transcript:
Header:
Date: 2025-01-14
Start time: 15:00 UTC
Duration: 47 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Lee (Redwood AE), Priya Nair (Redwood SE), Ethan Morales (Redwood CSM), Marta Ruiz (AmberGrid - Head of Data), Samir Patel (AmberGrid - ML Eng), Claire Donovan (AmberGrid - Security), Tom Briggs (AmberGrid - Product)

Summary Notes (auto): brief - regression spike on entity extraction, some guardrail false positives increased after last prompt tune, customer asks for Dedicated sim and security docs.

[00:00] Jordan: Okay, hi everyone, thanks for joining, uh we'll kick off, I'm Jordan Lee from Redwood. Quick roll call?
[00:06] Marta: Hey Marta here, Samir, Claire, Tom in the call.
[00:09] Priya: Priya Nair, SE on the call.
[00:11] Ethan: Ethan Morales, CSM.
[00:13] Tom: Tom Briggs, product.
[00:15] Jordan: Great, objective today is triage the regression report you sent and go over guardrail tuning plus a short security checklist. We have 47 mins. Sound good?
[00:25] Marta: Yes. quick comment - the entity extraction drift was visible after Friday's prompt update. We saw an uptick in hallucinations where the model made up meter IDs.
[00:34] Samir: Yeah, I can show an example - actually two. Claire, you'll want to hear this too.
[00:40] Claire: Please. security implications if the model invents identifiers that look like PII.
[00:46] [01:02] Priya: Can you remind me which prompt variant you rolled last week? The one labeled v3-b or v3-c? I think there was a tokenized prefix change.
[01:10] Samir: It's v3-b, we swapped the system prompt to be more permissive, and added the new extraction hinting. Maybe too permissive.
[01:18] Jordan: That matches the heatmap - precision dropped 7 points on the entity class meter_id. We have the regression sheet open, row 172 - see the pattern where the model invents five-digit ids. It's likely the hinting caused overgeneration.
[01:36] Marta: Right, our scoring uses F1 with weighted false positives more costly. So the observed drop is material for our SLAs.
[01:44] Ethan: Quick note - we recommended a conservative guardrail threshold last sprint, but that was for the hosted profile. If you move to Dedicated or change tokenization it can shift thresholds.
[01:55] [02:10] Tom: On Dedicated - we need cost delta numbers. The product team wants to know, like, if we commit to Dedicated for the pilot how much above hosted will it be.
[02:20] Jordan: We'll send a delta. Ballpark: Dedicated reserved instances for this profile are approx 20-30% higher in fixed monthly but reduce per-token unit cost under steady throughput. We'll get you a precise workbook.
[02:34] Marta: Also security - can you confirm KMS integration? We can't leak keys to an external provider.
[02:41] Priya: Yes, Redwood Private supports customer-managed KMS, HSMs for the private offering. For Hosted, we do envelope encryption and can integrate with your KMS via a connector in the private control plane. I'll share the config notes.
[02:54] Claire: Do you have SOC 2 artifact links? Our auditors want the last SOC 2 type II report.
[03:01] Jordan: I'll share the SOC 2 link and a redacted audit page. We also have an SOC2 + ISO summary deck.
[03:08] [03:20] Samir: Back to regressions - we ran a 1k sample overnight of user chats and scored on current rubric, attached the sheet. The bad cases cluster around non-standard meter formats and compound addresses.
[03:32] Priya: Ok, for next step I propose we: 1) revert the hinting in v3-b for meter_id, 2) add a strict regex post-filter for meter_id class before returning, 3) run the 2k regression set. Does that match everyone's appetite?
[03:47] Marta: Yes, regex filter seems low risk. But we worry about false negatives - losing legit new formats.
[03:55] Jordan: We can make the post-filter soft: tag low-confidence matches for human review rather than drop them. That reduces recall loss.
[04:03] [04:18] Tom: There were some guardrail blocks on neutral utterances last run - false positives where the safety rule flagged 'billing dispute' as policy escalation. That hurts UX.
[04:26] Priya: That's likely the thresholds on the safety classifier - we can loosen and then add targeted unit tests to catch the cases you mentioned.
[04:34] Samir: Will that open the door to real policy violations?
[04:38] Priya: We will scope a canary: loosen threshold but add an additional rule that catches true policy triggers with higher-cost checks (APIs to a secondary model, for example). So you get fewer false positives without losing true positives.
[04:52] Claire: From compliance side we need full audit logs for any auto-escallations and must ensure SSO is enforced for log access.
[04:59] Ethan: Redwood Console has token-level tracing and event logs; we'll share the retention options and RBAC mapping.
[05:08] [05:30] Marta: Samir ran a perf baseline too, it looks like median latency jumped in certain long conversation contexts. Could be KV cache thrashing?
[05:42] Priya: Correct - if the cache key cardinality is high because you include long prefixes, that can reduce cache hit rate. We recommend prefix trimming and a KV cache TTL of 4mins for your workload. But we'll validate in the Dedicated sim.
[05:56] Samir: How do we run the Dedicated sim? We need a window where we can push 100rps with real-ish payloads.
[06:03] Jordan: We'll schedule a 30-minute sim in a reserved pool, Redwood SE will coordinate IP whitelisting and a brief network test. Priya will run the perf harness.
[06:12] [06:30] Tom: One more ask - can you provide a quick rundown of how rollbacks work? If we deploy a prompt change and see regressions, what's the recommended rollback flow?
[06:38] Priya: We have version pinning per model and per route, canary rollout percentages, and an automatic fallback to a compatible model variant. So you can set a canary at 5% then 50, and if the guardrail fails we auto-fallback to the previous pinned version. We also keep per-token traces to audit the decision.
[06:58] [07:10] Marta: Great. On scoring - our rubric currently weights recall 0.6 and precision 0.4 for meter_id. Maybe we should tilt to precision given SLA.
[07:20] Jordan: Agreed, that's why the false positives are more costly for you. We can produce the eval curves and show how the F1/precision tradeoff moves with threshold.
[07:30] [07:45] Samir: A quick note - the dataset contains both free-text meter descriptions and structured reads. The hybrid examples seem to confuse the extractor.
[07:55] Priya: For hybrids we often separate the pipeline: structured-first extractor then fallback to NER. That reduces hallucinations. We'll prototype that in the next run.
[08:06] [08:20] Claire: Security question - will logs with extracted entities ever leave our VPC? We need them for debugging but can't have PII land in hosted buckets.
[08:28] Jordan: For Private we can keep logs inside your VPC. For Hosted we can configure obfuscation and minimal logging and push only redacted traces. We'll detail options in the doc.
[08:38] Marta: Okay action plan recap?
[08:42] Jordan: Yes recap: Priya revert hinting in v3-b and add regex soft filter; run 2k regression; Dedicated perf sim week of 1/20; Jordan to send SOC2 link and SOW draft; Samir to whitelist IPs; Marta to provide failure examples.
[08:58] [09:12] Tom: For the regression run, what's the acceptance threshold to consider the prompt change acceptable?
[09:18] Priya: Let's set a pass if precision for meter_id is not more than 2% below baseline and false positives decrease overall. We'll put the exact number in the rubric we share.
[09:29] Samir: Also we want a guardrail heatmap for false positives by intent - that helps us triage quickly.
[09:35] Priya: We'll add that to the report.
[09:39] [09:50] Claire: About SOC2 artifacts - we need certificate plus controls list and list of sub-processors.
[09:57] Jordan: I'll attach the SOC2 and a redacted sub-processor list.
[10:02] [10:20] Marta: One small product ask - can you include a per-call token estimate on the workbook? Our finance team wants line items.
[10:28] Jordan: We'll include estimated tokens per call, p50/p95.
[10:33] [10:40] Ethan: Ok we're at the security deep-dive we promised would be short. Claire any blocking items?
[10:46] Claire: We want confirmation on RBAC for log access and encryption endpoints. Also need retention policy options (30/90/365).
[10:55] Priya: We'll provide RBAC mapping examples and the retention config options.
[11:02] [11:20] Samir: Perf question - you mentioned kernel selection and quantization recommendations earlier. If we wanted cost reductions would quantize be safe for extraction tasks?
[11:29] Priya: For extractors, 4-bit quantization often preserves token-level accuracy when properly calibrated; but sequence-level tasks might regress slightly. We'll run quick A/B tests as part of the perf sim.
[11:42] [12:00] Jordan: Any other items before we close?
[12:05] Marta: No. thanks.
[12:08] Tom: Just confirm meeting notes and action items.
[12:11] Jordan: Will send notes, SOW draft, SOC2 link, and guardrail file by Friday.
[12:17] [12:25] Priya: I'll upload prompt variants and start the regression run once Marta's failure set is in.
[12:31] Jordan: Great, thanks everyone. We'll follow up in slack and schedule the Dedicated sim. Bye.
[12:36] End of recording.
